text:
lara: Putting up gossamer-embed-v0.9 on the staging board. Ran a small onboarding matrix: fp16, int8_perchannel, int4_perchannel, and a hybrid int4_fp16 projection. Short/medium holdouts (<=16 tokens, 17-64 tokens) and full wiki holdout.

lara: quick recall@5 (short): fp16=0.845, int8_pc=0.836, int4_pc=0.712, hybrid_int4_fp16=0.803. silhouette-score dropped for int4_pc.

diego: that int4 hit is large. Did you use bias correction / symmetric clipping during quant?

lara: default quant pipeline: per-channel min-max with clipping at 99.9 percentile, no bias correction. Ran a small variant with learned-scale asymmetric (LSQ-like) for int4_perchannel and it nudged R@5 to 0.735 on shortholdout.

sam: what's the embedding head? Are we projecting down with a linear layer before storage? dimension=1024 -> 256?

lara: yes: base model outputs 1024, we run a 256-d projection (trained). For the hybrid test we kept the projection weights in fp16 and quantized pre-projection activations to int4. That preserved ~95% of delta vs fp16.

anya: can you share the eval command + exact tokenizer/version so I can reproduce? short queries are sensitive to tokenization granularity.

lara: eval command used:
```
redwood-eval \
  --model gossamer-embed-v0.9 \
  --quant {fp16,int8_perchannel,int4_perchannel,hybrid_int4_fp16} \
  --holdouts /data/holdouts/short.json,/data/holdouts/medium.json,/data/holdouts/wiki.json \
  --metrics recall@1,5,10,ari,silhouette,avg_pos_cos,avg_neg_cos \
  --tokenizer roberta-v2.1 \
  --batch 128 \
  --seed 123
```

lara: note: we also tried whiten-before-proj vs whiten-after-proj. Int4 behaved markedly worse when whitening was applied after quantization.

sam: that aligns with theory: whitening can amplify quant noise if done after low-bit discretization. So norm/whiten order matters. Document that.

diego: any cluster-level metrics? ARI/cluster purity numbers?

lara: ARI (short): fp16=0.64, int8_pc=0.61, int4_pc=0.42, hybrid=0.59. silhouette: fp16=0.31, int4_pc=0.12.

anya: Oof. Did you try OPQ or PCA to compress instead of hard int4 quant on the output space? Sometimes product quantization reduces distortion for NN tasks.

lara: quick OPQ baseline: 256->64 OPQ + int8 storage, recall@5 short=0.798. So OPQ+int8 could be a good tradeoff vs pure int4 storage.

sam: good. Also capture throughput and KNN recall-latency curve; int4 storage helps memory but can require dequant+dot on the fly which kills latency if not using optimized kernels.

lara: added perf runs: k=5 latency (ms) ~ fp16=12.4, int8_pc_store=9.1, int4_pc_store=7.2 (but note indexing used scalar dequant in Python -> hybrid optimized C kernel pending). Hybrid where projection remains fp16 and only pre-proj is int4 gives latency ~9.5ms.

ci-bot: CI: artifact upload complete. Links: s3://redwood-artifacts/eng-ml/gossamer/v0.9/boards/3890011222/{plots,configs,raw_metrics}.tar.gz

diego: recommend path forward: 1) block int4_perchannel for short-query SLA until we have optimized dequant kernel + bias-correction sweep; 2) prefer hybrid_int4_fp16 or OPQ+int8 for now; 3) add a short-query "anchor stability" test to the onboarding checklist with tokenizer pinned.

anya: also add a multilingual micro-holdout (en/es/zh) and a small noise-perturbation test (typos, concat small clauses) since low-bit transforms sometimes collapse these neighbors.

lara: ack. I'll draft the PR to update onboarding docs and include the artifacts + commands + seeds. Will also open a perf ticket for optimized int4 dequant kernel.

sam: capture exact tokenization stats too (avg tokens per query in each holdout) 12 vs 3 tokens can flip results.

lara: uploaded tokenization histograms to the artifact bundle. I'll post a short summary in #embed-failures when PR is up.

ci-bot: Staging autoscaler: scaled eng-ml-staging +1 node (eval sweep) at 2026-04-07T11:07:50Z

lara: Thanks all. Plan: block int4 storage flag in model catalog for gossamer-embed-v0.9 until we validate bias-correction + kernel. Will proceed with hybrid/OPQ alternatives for the Dedicated cost workstream. :rocket:
